mainTopic: An unfaithful wife's worn items, the כתובה of an אילונית and of a widow married to a כהן גדול, and the new chapter on a husband's promise to feed his wife's daughter
overview: The amud opens by finishing a line about a wife keeping her own worn items (בלאות) that still exist. A תנא recites a ברייתא saying an unfaithful wife loses them. רב נחמן objects that her clothes did not sin and corrects the wording, while רבי יוחנן says that ברייתא is only the view of רבי מנחם סתימתאה. Next, רב הונא says an אילונית gets a כתובה only if the husband knew about her condition, but a widow married to a כהן גדול gets one either way. רב יהודה says the widow also needs the husband to have known. Two ברייתות refute רב הונא, and the גמרא explains how the wording of the משנה misled him. The chapter אלמנה ניזונת then ends, and a new chapter opens with a משנה about a husband who promised to feed his wife's daughter for five years. That promise works like a real debt: it binds a second husband too, survives divorce, and can even be collected from property he sold. The גמרא brings a dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about someone who wrote 'I owe you a מנה' in a שטר with no witnesses. It then starts to test that dispute against our משנה.

steps.title: End of the line about her existing worn items
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the previous statement: her worn items that still exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: …her worn items that still exist.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a sentence that started earlier: the woman still gets back her own worn items that still exist. This sets up the next discussion about whether a woman can lose them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלאות are the clothes and household items a woman brought into the marriage that wore out but still exist. The point is that she does not lose them, because they are still hers. The next step asks whether a woman who was unfaithful is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Worn-out items, mainly the wife's clothing and belongings
Still in existence

phrases.english: her worn items that still exist.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: she does not lose her worn items that still exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman keeps her own worn items that still exist.

steps.title: A ברייתא says an unfaithful wife loses her worn items
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רב נחמן: if she זינתה, she loses her existing worn items.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא recited before רב נחמן: If she was unfaithful, she loses her worn items that still exist.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא, a person who memorized ברייתות, recites one in front of רב נחמן. It says a wife who was unfaithful loses even her own worn items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman gets back her own worn items when the marriage ends. This ברייתא adds a penalty: an unfaithful wife loses even those. That makes it sound like her own property is taken away as a punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (someone who memorized and recited ברייתות) recited
She was unfaithful (had relations with another man)
She lost (her right to something)

phrases.english: A tanna recited before Rav Naḥman:
phrases.notes: Here a תנא is a person whose job was to memorize ברייתות and recite them in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: If she was unfaithful, she loses her worn items that still exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with an exception to the rule that she keeps her worn items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this ברייתא, a wife who was unfaithful loses her existing worn items.

steps.title: רב נחמן objects that her clothes did not sin
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks: if she sinned, did her clothing sin?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If she was unfaithful, were her belongings unfaithful?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the ברייתא. Her clothes are her property, and they did nothing wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her sin may cost her the money from her כתובה, but these items are simply hers. There is no reason to take away something she owns. So the ruling in the ברייתא does not make sense to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Her belongings or clothing
Were they unfaithful? (a question that expects the answer 'no')

phrases.english: He said to him:
If she was unfaithful,
were her belongings unfaithful?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם הִיא זִינְּתָה, כֵּלֶיהָ מִי זַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of the ברייתא from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that an unfaithful wife loses her worn items.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her sin does not change who owns her property. The belongings did nothing wrong, so there is no reason she should lose them.

steps.title: רב נחמן changes the wording to 'she does not lose'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells the תנא: recite it as 'she does not lose her existing worn items.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Recite it this way: She does not lose her worn items that still exist.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן fixes the problem by telling the תנא to change the wording of the ברייתא. It should say she does NOT lose her worn items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of accepting a ruling that makes no sense, רב נחמן decides the ברייתא was recited wrong. With the new wording, the ברייתא now agrees with simple logic: her sin does not take away her own property.

keyTerms.meaning: Recite it (this way): used to correct the wording of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying there are two opinions here. He is saying the ברייתא itself was recited wrong and must be changed.

phrases.english: Recite:
She does not lose her worn items that still exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the objection of step 3 by changing the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as recited said an unfaithful wife loses her worn items.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is that she does not lose them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא follows רבי מנחם סתימתאה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: the ברייתא is the view of רבי מנחם סתימתאה, but the חכמים say she does not lose her worn items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the view of רבי מנחם סתימתאה. But the חכמים say: If she was unfaithful, she does not lose her worn items that still exist.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a different way to handle the ברייתא. Instead of changing its wording, רבי יוחנן says it is the opinion of one תנא, and the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the original wording was a mistake. רבי יוחנן keeps the original wording but calls it a minority opinion, the view of רבי מנחם סתימתאה. Both approaches end up with the same הלכה: the חכמים rule that she keeps her worn items.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose name is often left out of teachings, so he is called 'the unnamed one'
But the חכמים (the majority of scholars) say

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן agree on the הלכה: an unfaithful wife still keeps her own worn items. They differ only on how to explain the ברייתא that said otherwise.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Menaḥem the unnamed one,
phrases.notes: 'This' refers to the ברייתא from step 2 saying she loses her worn items.

phrases.english: but the Rabbis say:
If she was unfaithful, she does not lose her worn items that still exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מְנַחֵם סְתִימְתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Handles the ברייתא differently from רב נחמן: it belongs to a minority opinion instead of being changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא follows רבי מנחם סתימתאה; the חכמים rule that an unfaithful wife keeps her existing worn items.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה about marrying an אילונית knowingly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: 'If from the start he married her…'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If from the start he married her…' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about a man who married an אילונית knowing about her condition. This sets up רב הונא's statement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if he knew from the start that she was an אילונית, she does get a כתובה. The גמרא quotes just the opening words with כו׳ to point to that line before commenting on it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start
He married her
And so on: the quote continues as in the משנה

phrases.english: 'If from the start he married her,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: if he knew she was an אילונית when he married her, she gets a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of בלאות and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Points back to the משנה's ruling that an אילונית married knowingly gets a כתובה.

steps.title: רב הונא: an אילונית is partly a wife, a widow is a full wife
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: an אילונית is 'a wife and not a wife'; a widow is 'a complete wife.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: An אילונית is a wife and is not a wife. A widow is a complete wife.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא compares two women from the משנה. An אילונית is only partly treated as a wife, while a widow married to a כהן גדול is treated as a full wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow married to a כהן גדול is in a forbidden marriage, yet רב הונא calls her a complete wife. An אילונית is in a permitted marriage, yet he calls her only partly a wife, because the marriage may rest on a mistake about her condition. The גמרא will go on to explain what practical difference this makes.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who cannot have children and does not develop normally
A wife and not a wife: only partly treated as a wife
Widow (here, one married to a כהן גדול)
A complete, full wife

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the forbidden marriage (widow to a כהן גדול) is the weaker one. רב הונא says the widow is the full wife, and the אילונית is the partial one.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
An ailonit is a wife and is not a wife,
a widow is a complete wife.
phrases.notes: He means the widow from the משנה who married a כהן גדול, even though that marriage is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אַיְלוֹנִית אִשָּׁה וְאֵינָהּ אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the line of the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אילונית has only partial status as a wife, while a widow married to a כהן גדול has full status as a wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the סוגיא, which works out what practical difference there is between being 'partly' and 'fully' a wife.

steps.title: רב הונא spells out his rule: knowing matters for an אילונית but not for a widow
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains his rule. An אילונית gets a כתובה only if the husband knew about her condition. A widow married to a כהן גדול gets a כתובה whether he knew or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אילונית is a wife and not a wife: if he knew about her, she has a כתובה; if he did not know about her, she has no כתובה. A widow is a complete wife: whether he knew about her or did not know about her, she has a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא continues his statement from the previous step and explains what 'a wife and not a wife' and 'a complete wife' actually mean in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an אילונית, everything depends on the husband's knowledge. If he knew, she gets her כתובה. If he didn't know, the marriage was a mistake on his side and she gets nothing. A widow is different: her כתובה does not depend on whether he knew.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is physically unable to have children
He knew about her (her condition) before the marriage
A widow (here, one married to a כהן גדול, who is forbidden to marry her)
A complete wife, fully treated as a wife for her כתובה
The marriage contract payment a wife receives at divorce or the husband's death

phrases.english: An ailonit is a wife and not a wife:
if he knew about her, she has a marriage contract;
phrases.notes: "Knew about her" means he knew before the wedding that she was an אילונית.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ — אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: if he did not know about her, she has no marriage contract.
A widow is a complete wife:
phrases.notes: This is the widow married to a כהן גדול from the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הִכִּיר בָּהּ, בֵּין לֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ —
phrases.english: whether he knew about her or did not know about her,
she has a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical meaning of רב הונא's short statement in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אילונית gets a כתובה only if the husband knew. A widow married to a כהן גדול gets a כתובה either way.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the widow is also judged by whether he knew
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה disagrees with רב הונא about the widow. He says both the אילונית and the widow get a כתובה only if the husband knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה says: both this one and that one are a wife and not a wife. If he knew about her, she has a כתובה; if he did not know about her, she has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a competing view. He treats the widow exactly like the אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two אמוראים agree about the אילונית. They argue only about the widow. רב יהודה says a widow also loses her כתובה if the כהן גדול did not know she was a widow.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב הונא here
Both this one and that one (the אילונית and the widow)

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda says:
both this one and that one
phrases.notes: He means both the אילונית and the widow.

phrases.english: are a wife and not a wife.
If he knew about her, she has a marriage contract;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ — אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: if he did not know about her, she has no marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a disagreeing view on the widow half of רב הונא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both an אילונית and a widow married to a כהן גדול get a כתובה only if the husband knew.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say an unspecified marriage gives no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא. If a man married a woman knowing about her issue, she gets a כתובה. That seems to imply that if nothing was said, she gets no כתובה, even a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: if he married her assuming she was so, and she turned out to be so, she has a כתובה. This implies that if he married her without specifying, she has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב הונא's view that a widow gets a כתובה even when the husband did not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a כתובה only when he married her already knowing her situation. From this the גמרא infers that in a plain marriage, where nothing was known or said, she gets nothing. That contradicts רב הונא, who said a widow gets a כתובה even when he didn't know.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged: a formal objection from a תנאי source
On the assumption that
But this implies: in an unspecified case

phrases.english: They challenged:
If he married her on the assumption that she is so,
phrases.notes: "So" means having the issue, like being an אילונית or a widow forbidden to him.

phrases.english: and she is found to be so,
she has a marriage contract.
This implies: if unspecified, she has no marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's rule about the widow from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a widow gets a כתובה even if the husband did not know
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא grants a כתובה only when he knew. By inference, an unspecified marriage gives no כתובה, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: Read the inference differently: only 'assumed she was fine' loses the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's inference is not about an unspecified marriage. It is about a man who married her assuming she had no issue. On this answer the ברייתא says nothing about the plain unspecified case, so רב הונא can still be right. Steps 12 and 13 go on to reject this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say that in an unspecified case she has no כתובה. Rather say: if he married her assuming she is not so, and she turned out to be so, she has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by changing what we learn from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opposite of 'he assumed she had the issue' is not 'nothing was said.' It is 'he assumed she did NOT have the issue.' Only that case loses the כתובה. The ordinary unspecified marriage of a widow is not addressed, so רב הונא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say
Rather, say
That she is not so (does not have the issue)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing the ברייתא's words. It is only changing what we infer from them, swapping 'unspecified' for 'he assumed she was fine.'
steps.whatToRemember: An inference from a ברייתא can be read in more than one way. Here, the opposite of 'he knew about her issue' is 'he assumed she had no issue,' not 'nothing was said.' That keeps רב הונא's view intact.

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא: הָא סְתָמָא אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה,
phrases.english: Do not say: this implies that if unspecified she has no marriage contract,
rather, say:
if he married her on the assumption that she is not so,
and she is found to be so,
she has no marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא: הָא סְתָמָא אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by re-reading the ברייתא's implication.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the inference (changing what is implied, not the text itself)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies that an unspecified marriage gives no כתובה, against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only implies that a man who assumed she had no issue owes no כתובה. On this answer the ברייתא does not address the unspecified case, so רב הונא stands for now. Steps 12 and 13 reject this answer.

steps.title: The earlier defense of רב הונא does not hold up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer from Step 11. If an unspecified marriage really gave a כתובה, the ברייתא should have taught that case, since the 'knew about it' case would then be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about an unspecified case? If she gets a כתובה there, then instead of teaching 'he married her presuming she was like this, and she turned out like this, so she gets a כתובה,' the ברייתא should have taught the unspecified case. Then we would know this case all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the answer it just gave in Step 11 in defense of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the גמרא said the unspecified case was left open, so רב הונא might be right. Now it argues: if the unspecified case also gets a כתובה, the ברייתא picked the less useful case to teach. Teaching the unspecified case would have covered the 'he knew' case automatically, so the ברייתא's choice suggests the unspecified case gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: An unspecified case, where nothing was said about her status
Instead of teaching
With the presumption that she is like this
All the more so

phrases.english: But in an unspecified case, what is the law?
She has [a marriage contract]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about the answer from Step 11: if the plain case also gets a כתובה...

phrases.english: Instead of teaching 'with the presumption that she is so'

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצֵאת שֶׁהִיא כֵּן יֵשׁ לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה,
phrases.english: and she was found to be so, she has a marriage contract,
let it teach us the unspecified case,
and all the more so this one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 11 answer that the ברייתא leaves the unspecified case open
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא should teach the bigger new idea. If the unspecified case also gets a כתובה, the ברייתא should have taught that case, and the 'he knew' case would follow by כל שכן.

steps.title: A ברייתא says it outright: no כתובה when nothing was said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says clearly that an unspecified marriage gives no כתובה. This is declared a full refutation of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, a ברייתא teaches: If he married her knowing about her issue, and she was found to have that known issue, she has a כתובה. If he married her without anything said, she has no כתובה. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger attack: a ברייתא that says the unspecified case directly, so no inference is needed. It ends by declaring רב הונא refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 needed an inference from the ברייתא, and Step 11 tried to get around it. This ברייתא states the unspecified case openly: no כתובה. That directly contradicts רב הונא, who said a widow gets a כתובה even when the husband did not know.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which brings an additional proof
Knowingly, with her issue known
Without anything said
A full refutation of an אמורא's view

steps.whatToRemember: With רב הונא refuted, the view left standing is רב יהודה's: if the husband did not know, even a widow married to a כהן גדול gets no כתובה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught:
If he married her knowingly and she was found as was known,
she has a marriage contract;
if he married her without specification, she has no marriage contract.
This is a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, explicit source on top of the argument in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule in Step 8 that a widow gets a כתובה even when the husband did not know
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says outright that an unspecified marriage gives no כתובה, which directly contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: How רב הונא misread the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב הונא made his mistake. He thought the משנה split the cases only for the אילונית, but really that split applies to the widow too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה misled רב הונא. He thought: since the משנה makes a distinction for the אילונית but not for the widow, it must mean a widow gets a כתובה even in an unspecified case. But that is not so. When the משנה teaches about the widow, it relies on the distinction it already made for the אילונית.
steps.whatsHappening: After refuting רב הונא, the גמרא explains how he came to his mistaken view, which wraps up the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states the 'knew or did not know' distinction only for the אילונית. רב הונא read this as meaning the widow has no such distinction and always gets a כתובה. The גמרא says the distinction for the אילונית carries over to the widow as well, so the widow also gets a כתובה only if the husband knew.

keyTerms.meaning: Misled him
Makes a distinction between cases
By implication, from this we learn
But that is not so
Stands on, relies on

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא was not ignoring the משנה. He was reading it too closely, and the silence about the widow is what misled him.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'did he know?' distinction stated for the אילונית applies to the widow too.

phrases.english: The mishna misled Rav Huna.
He thought: since it distinguishes with an ailonit
and does not distinguish with a widow,
this implies that a widow
even in an unspecified case also has [a marriage contract].
But that is not so:
when it teaches the case of the widow,
it relies on the distinction made for the ailonit.
phrases.notes: He means the 'knew or didn't know' split stated for the אילונית also covers the widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation, the גמרא explains where רב הונא's mistake came from.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's distinction for the אילונית applies to the widow too. A widow married to a כהן גדול gets a כתובה only if he knew.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing אלמנה ניזונת
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter אלמנה ניזונת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'אלמנה ניזונת.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'Hadran' formula marks that this chapter of כתובות is finished, and it expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula for a chapter
'A widow is provided for,' the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'A widow is provided for.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the sugya ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the chapter אלמנה ניזונת.

steps.title: A husband who agreed to feed his wife's daughter must do so
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens: a man who agreed, when he married, to feed his wife's daughter for five years is bound to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man marries a woman and she makes a deal with him that he will feed her daughter for five years, he must feed the girl for five years.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It sets the basic rule: a promise made at the wedding to feed the wife's daughter is binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter is not his own child. Normally he would owe her nothing. His agreement with the mother creates a real obligation for the full five years.

keyTerms.meaning: She set terms, made a binding deal
To feed her, to provide her food
Her daughter (here, from a previous husband)

steps.whyThisMatters: This basic case is the foundation for every rule that follows in the משנה and the chapter.

phrases.english: One who marries a woman
and she made a deal with him

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּזוּן אֶת בִּתָּהּ חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים
phrases.english: that he would feed her daughter for five years
phrases.notes: This is her daughter from an earlier husband, not his own child.

phrases.english: he is obligated to feed her for five years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the closing line of אלמנה ניזונת in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband's promise to feed his wife's daughter for five years is binding.

steps.title: A second husband who makes the same deal is also fully bound
steps.stepSummary: If the woman remarries and the new husband makes the same promise, he also owes the full five years. The first husband must deliver the food to the girl where her mother lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she then marries another man and makes the same deal with him, he too must feed the girl for five years. The first husband cannot say, 'I'll feed her only if she comes to my house.' He has to bring her food to wherever her mother lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second husband who made the same promise. It rules that both obligations stand, and that the first husband must deliver the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second husband's promise does not cancel the first husband's promise. Each one owes the full amount. The first husband also cannot set a condition that makes it hard for the girl to collect. She lives with her mother, so the food goes there.

keyTerms.meaning: She married another man
The first husband
He brings, delivers
Food, support

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second husband's promise frees the first one. Both owe her food in full.

phrases.english: If she married another man
phrases.notes: This means she was divorced from the first husband during those five years.

phrases.english: and she made a deal with him

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּזוּן אֶת בִּתָּהּ חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים
phrases.english: that he would feed her daughter for five years
he is obligated to feed her for five years.
The first husband may not say:
When she comes to me, I will feed her
rather, he brings her food to her
to the place where her mother is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the basic case to a second husband who makes the same promise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both husbands are fully bound, and the first must deliver the food to where the girl lives with her mother.

steps.title: The two husbands cannot share one portion of food
steps.stepSummary: The two men cannot team up and feed her together. One gives her actual food and the other gives her its value in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, the two of them cannot say, 'We'll feed her together.' Instead, one feeds her and the other gives her the money that food would cost.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה blocks the two husbands from combining their obligations into one shared portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man promised a full five years of food. If they shared, each would really be paying only half. So the girl gets two full portions: real food from one and its cash value from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Together, as one
The money value of food

phrases.english: And likewise, the two of them may not say:
"We will feed her together"
rather, one feeds her
and the other gives her the money value of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit on the two husbands, building on the fact that both are fully bound.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each husband pays in full. One gives food and the other gives its value in money.

steps.title: If the daughter marries, both men still pay
steps.stepSummary: If the girl marries, her own husband feeds her, and the two men still give her the money value of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the girl gets married, her husband gives her food, and the two men give her the money value of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה covers the case where the daughter herself marries during the five years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once married, her husband must feed her, so she no longer needs their food. Their promise still stands, though, so they pay her its value in cash.

keyTerms.meaning: Her husband (the daughter's own husband)
She married (here, the daughter)

steps.confusionAlert: In this step, נִיסֵּת is about the daughter, not the mother.

phrases.english: If she got married
phrases.notes: Now it's the daughter who marries.

phrases.english: her husband gives her food
and they give her the money value of food.
phrases.notes: "They" are the mother's two husbands who made the promise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two men's obligation to a new situation: the daughter's own marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter's marriage does not cancel the promise. The two men pay her the value of food.

steps.title: After the men die, she collects like a creditor
steps.stepSummary: If the men die, their own daughters are fed only from property still in the estate. The stepdaughter can collect even from property they sold, because she is like a creditor.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the men die, their own daughters are fed only from property that was not sold. She, however, is fed even from property they had sold, because she is like someone who is owed a debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by comparing the stepdaughter's rights after the men die with the rights of their own daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man's own daughters are fed from his estate, but only from property he still owned. The stepdaughter's support comes from a deal he made, so it counts as a debt. A creditor can take back property the debtor sold after the debt was created, so she can collect even from sold property.

keyTerms.meaning: Free property, still owned and not sold
Liened property, already sold but still tied to a debt
A creditor, someone who is owed money

steps.whatToRemember: A promise to feed a stepdaughter is a real debt. Each promiser pays in full, delivers to where she lives, keeps paying even after she marries, and owes her even from property he sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a deal made at the wedding is stronger than the built-in rights of his own daughters. It works like a loan.

phrases.english: If they died
phrases.notes: "They" are the two husbands who promised to feed her.

phrases.english: their own daughters are fed from free property
and she is fed even from liened property
phrases.notes: This means property the men sold to others after making the promise.

phrases.english: because she is like a creditor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתוּ בְּנוֹתֵיהֶן נִיזּוֹנוֹת מִנְּכָסִים בְּנֵי חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה by covering the men's deaths and how the stepdaughter collects from their estates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stepdaughter collects even from sold property, because her claim is a debt, while the men's own daughters collect only from unsold property.

steps.title: Clever husbands limited the promise
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes by teaching that smart husbands wrote that they would feed the wife's daughter for five years only as long as the wife stays married to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The clever ones would write: 'On condition that I feed your daughter for five years, as long as you are with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with practical advice: clever husbands wrote a limit into their promise so it ends if the marriage ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps showed that the promise stays in force even after a divorce, and can even be collected after death. By adding 'as long as you are with me,' the husband avoids feeding a girl who is not his daughter once he is no longer married to her mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Clever, sharp-thinking people
On condition that
That I will feed or support
As long as you are with me, meaning while we are married

steps.whatToRemember: The basic promise to feed the wife's daughter has no built-in time limit tied to the marriage. A wise husband adds 'as long as you are with me.'

phrases.english: The clever ones would write:
"On condition that I feed your daughter

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאַתְּ עִמִּי.
phrases.english: for five years, as long as you are with me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה with practical advice on avoiding the long-term obligations described in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband can limit his promise to feed his wife's daughter so that it lasts only while he stays married to her mother.

steps.title: Dispute over saying 'I owe you a מנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a מחלוקת. If a person says 'I owe you a מנה,' רבי יוחנן says he must pay and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated: If someone says to his friend, 'I owe you a מנה,' רבי יוחנן says he must pay, and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a dispute about a person who admits that he owes money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether simply saying 'I owe you' is enough to make a person pay. רבי יוחנן says the admission obligates him. ריש לקיש says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, which introduces a dispute between אמוראים
A set amount of money, one hundred dinars
Obligated, he must pay
Exempt, he does not have to pay

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
One who says to his fellow,
"I owe you a מָנֶה"
Rabbi Yochanan said: he must pay.
And Reish Lakish said: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion with a new dispute after the משנה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: saying 'I owe you a מנה' obligates payment. ריש לקיש: it does not.

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case. If he said 'you are my witnesses,' why would ריש לקיש exempt him? If he did not say it, why would רבי יוחנן obligate him?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he told them 'you are my witnesses,' what is ריש לקיש's reason for exempting him? If he did not tell them 'you are my witnesses,' what is רבי יוחנן's reason for obligating him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the dispute is about, because both obvious cases seem too simple to argue over. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he formally named witnesses, everyone should agree he must pay, so ריש לקיש's view is hard to understand. If he did not name witnesses, his words could be a casual remark, so רבי יוחנן's view is hard to understand. The גמרא needs a middle case where both sides make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the details of the case?
'You are my witnesses,' a formal way of making an admission binding
What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he said to them, "You are my witnesses,"
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the people standing nearby when he spoke.

phrases.english: what is the reason of Reish Lakish, who exempts him?
If he did not say to them, "You are my witnesses,"
what is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan, who obligates him?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דְּאָמַר לְהוּ ״אַתֶּם עֵדַיי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case of the dispute in step 22, showing that each simple version makes one side hard to understand.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific case in which both רבי יוחנן's and ריש לקיש's positions make sense.
steps.kashyaTarget: The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either version of the case seems to make one opinion obviously wrong.

steps.title: The case is an admission written in a שטר without witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where he did not name witnesses, but wrote 'I owe you a מנה' in a שטר that has no witnesses on it. רבי יוחנן holds that putting it in a שטר makes his words as strong as naming witnesses, and ריש לקיש disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he did not say 'you are my witnesses.' The case is where he said, 'I owe you a מנה by a שטר.' רבי יוחנן says he must pay, because mentioning a שטר is strong, like saying 'you are witnesses.' ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because mentioning a שטר is not strong enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he did not name witnesses, but he gave his admission in a written שטר with no witnesses. The dispute is about how much that writing adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a plain spoken admission without naming witnesses would not be enough. The question is whether writing the admission in a שטר, even one without witnesses, makes it serious enough. רבי יוחנן says it counts like naming witnesses, and ריש לקיש says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually, which keeps one side of the question and adds a detail
Here, what are we dealing with? This introduces a more specific case
With or in a written document
The matter is strong, meaning it carries legal weight

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about an admission made without naming witnesses but written in a שטר that has no witnesses. רבי יוחנן: the שטר makes it as binding as naming witnesses. ריש לקיש: it does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן holds that any casual 'I owe you' obligates. The גמרא explains that he obligates only because the admission was put in a שטר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question of the dispute: what gives spoken words enough weight to create a binding debt.

phrases.english: Really, it is where he did not say to them, "You are my witnesses,"
and here, what are we dealing with?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ ״חַיָּיב אֲנִי לְךָ מָנֶה בִּשְׁטָר״.
phrases.english: Where he said to him, "I owe you a מָנֶה by a document."
phrases.notes: The new detail is that he put it in writing, in a document with no witnesses signed on it. That is what the two אמוראים argue about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: he must pay,
because something said with a document is strong,
and it is like one who said to them, "You are witnesses."
Reish Lakish said: he is exempt,
because something said with a document is not strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא קָאָמַר לְהוּ ״אַתֶּם עֵדַיי״, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by choosing the case without witnesses and adding the detail of a שטר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is where he did not name witnesses but wrote that he owes the money in a שטר without witnesses. The dispute is whether such a שטר is as strong as naming witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute seemed to be either with witnesses named or without, and both seemed too simple to argue over.
steps.terutzMaskana: No witnesses were named, but the admission was written in a שטר. רבי יוחנן treats that as strong and ריש לקיש does not.

steps.title: Does the משנה about feeding the stepdaughter prove רבי יוחנן right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a man who agreed to feed his wife's daughter for five years must feed her. It asks whether this is the same kind of case as 'I owe you a מנה in a שטר,' which would support רבי יוחנן against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: One who marries a woman, and she arranged with him that he would feed her daughter for five years, must feed her for five years. Isn't the משנה talking about a case just like this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge against ריש לקיש from our own משנה. It suggests that the משנה's case matches the case of 'I owe you in a שטר,' where the man is bound only by his own written commitment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the husband's duty to feed the girl comes only from what he agreed to. If that agreement was written without proper witnesses and he must still pay, his written word alone obligates him, just as רבי יוחנן says. That would be a problem for ריש לקיש, who says such a statement does not obligate.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
She arranged with him; they set a deal
To feed / support
Isn't it that...? (a leading question that pushes a proof)
In a case like this one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about the stepdaughter. The גמרא reuses the משנה only to test the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: We learned: One who marries a woman
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה, the one about feeding the wife's daughter.

phrases.aramaic: וּפָסְקָה עִמּוֹ לָזוּן אֶת בִּתָּהּ חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים,
phrases.english: and she arranged with him to feed her daughter for five years,
he must feed her for five years.
Isn't it in a case like this one?
phrases.notes: 'Like this one' means the case from the previous step: a commitment written in a שטר without naming witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 24 defines the case of the מחלוקת, this step attacks ריש לקיש's side using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that 'I owe you a מנה in a שטר' does not obligate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה obligates a husband based only on his agreement. If that agreement was a written commitment like the one in the מחלוקת, the משנה supports רבי יוחנן and goes against ריש לקיש.
